LanguageData.OWT_SettingSelfServiceDesc: Customers will buy from an unattended counter instead of walking out. Convenient, but a customer nobody served thinks only half as well of the town as one who was looked after.
LanguageData.OWT_CmdEvictGuestDesc: Release this bed's current guest immediately. They lose the room they already paid for — a guest evicted this way won't come back to this hotel for the rest of their visit.
LanguageData.OWT_CmdOpenDesc: When open, customers may browse and buy from this counter. Closing it does not stop your colonists using the room.
LanguageData.OWT_CmdCollectDesc: Empty the till onto the floor beside the counter, where a hauler can pick it up.
LanguageData.OWT_CmdLedgerDesc: How the town is trading: what its appeal is made of and what raises it, the town's name, today's business, and every shop's takings.
LanguageData.OWT_LedgerAppealLine: Appeal: {0} — how much trade the town attracts. Customers start arriving at 0.5. How often they come stops improving at 4.0; how many come keeps climbing past it. It is these three, multiplied:
LanguageData.OWT_LedgerAppealBusinessesLine: Businesses: {0}. A kind of business the town does not have yet is worth its full draw; each further one of a kind you already run is worth 35% of the one before it. A second counter of a kind you already sell, on a floor you already trade from, is a second till rather than a second business — it lets you serve two customers at once, and adds nothing here. A counter of a different kind on that floor is a new trade, and does count.
LanguageData.OWT_LedgerAppealGoodsLine: On offer: {0} — x{1}. Goods at market value, plus what a business that sells time rather than things is reckoned to be worth. Four times the goods for twice the draw, and every stack counts once however many counters can see it. What you charge does not count: appeal is what the town offers, not what it asks.
LanguageData.OWT_LedgerAppealMissingLine: Nothing on offer from a {0} right now — either the town has none, or the one it has is closed or bare. A trade you don't run at all is worth far more than another of one you do.
LanguageData.OWT_LedgerPurseLine: Customer purses: x{0} — set by the goods on offer alone, not by appeal. Breadth and a good name bring more travellers; a richer shelf brings travellers who can afford it.
LanguageData.OWT_LedgerReputationLine: Reputation: {0} — the town's service record. Every caller leaves one verdict a day, however much they bought: being served by somebody is worth full marks, taking goods off an unwatched counter half, and giving up waiting halves whatever else their day was worth. It sways how many travellers come (a good name brings half again as much custom as a neutral one, a bad name half as much) and what they'll pay (up to 10% either way).
LanguageData.OWT_LedgerTodayLine: Today: {0} came to a counter, {1} of them gave up waiting, {2} taken.
LanguageData.OWT_LedgerServiceLine: Service today: {0}. The town's name moves toward that tonight — putting somebody behind a counter now still changes it.
LanguageData.OWT_LedgerQuietLine: Nobody has come to a counter today; the town's name drifts back toward the middle.
LanguageData.OWT_LedgerRegularLine: Customers from {0} have become regulars ({1} standing).
LanguageData.OWT_LedgerColdLine: Customers from {0} want nothing more to do with this town ({1} standing).
LanguageData.OWT_TabStockShelves: On the shelves: {0} — {1} at market, {2} here
LanguageData.OWT_TabStockShelvesTip: What this counter has out: what those goods would fetch at market value, and what it is asking for them. On the shelves means out on this counter's sales floor — the room it stands in, or the ground around it if it stands outdoors — and allowed by the list below. Anything forbidden, or already claimed by one of your own haulers, is not for sale.
LanguageData.OWT_MarkupSliderTip: What this business charges, as a percentage of an item's market value. Cheaper shops win customers away from rivals; dearer ones make more per sale.
LanguageData.OWT_TabStockReputation: The town's name means customers pay {0}.
LanguageData.OWT_ReasonBusy: two customers are already headed there
LanguageData.OWT_LetterCustomersText: {0} travellers from {1} have heard there is business to be done here, and have come to spend.\n\nThey will browse whatever your open shops have on display and pay across the counter — if there is someone there to serve them.
LanguageData.OWT_CustomersScared: Violence in town. The customers from {0} are leaving.
LanguageData.OWT_CustomerWalkedOut: {0} gave up waiting at {1} and left the goods behind. They think the less of the town for it, and won't go back to that counter until somebody is standing behind it.
LanguageData.OWT_CustomerWalkedOutService: {0} gave up waiting at {1} and left. They think the less of the town for it, and won't go back to that counter until somebody is standing behind it.
LanguageData.OWT_ColonistGaveUp: {0} gave up waiting for a {1} at {2}. Nobody came to work the counter — raise Shopkeeping's priority, or right-click the counter with another colonist to send them to it. It cost the town nothing, and {0} the better part of an hour.
LanguageData.OWT_ColonistNotReached: {0} gave up waiting for a {1} at {2}. The counter was busy with other customers the whole time — it serves one at a time, so a second one is what would have fitted {0} in. It cost the town nothing, and {0} a few hours.
LanguageData.OWT_CounterBusy: Customers are walking past {0} rather than wait — a counter serves one at a time. Nobody was neglected and the town's name is untouched; what it costs is the sale. Another counter with somebody behind it is what turns them back into money.
LanguageData.OWT_GuestEvicted: {0}'s room at {1} was taken from them. Word of the poor treatment spreads.
LanguageData.OWT_AlertUnattendedDesc: Customers are queueing at a counter with nobody behind it. If a colonist with the Shopkeeping work type doesn't serve them soon, they will walk out — losing you the sale and hurting the town's reputation.
LanguageData.OWT_FalseFrontIdle: No open shop nearby to advertise for
LanguageData.OWT_CmdAssignSheriffDesc: Assign a colonist to hold this post as sheriff. While they're on duty here, patrons town-wide get rowdy more slowly, and the sheriff can step in to calm a specific patron down before they cause a disturbance.
LanguageData.OWT_PostAlreadyFilled: This post is already filled. Unassign its current holder first.
LanguageData.OWT_SaloonTrouble: {0} caused a scene at {1}. Word of the disturbance spreads, and they've had enough for one visit.
LanguageData.OWT_AlertRowdyPatronsDesc: A patron is getting loud. If nothing steps in, it will turn into a disturbance — losing you their custom for the rest of their visit and hurting the town's reputation. An assigned, on-duty sheriff can calm them down first.
LanguageData.OWT_CmdHouseEdgeDesc: Set how much of every wager the house expects to keep on average. A low edge keeps the table fair and patrons happy; a high one wins the house more per hand but pays out less often, and angers losers faster.
LanguageData.OWT_CheatingAccusation: {0} accuses the dealer at {1} of cheating after a bad hand.
LanguageData.OWT_HouseCantCover: {0} won big at {1}, but the house can only cover {2} of the {3} owed. The table closes its doors until someone reopens it.
LanguageData.OWT_CmdCollectDescWager: Empty the till onto the floor beside the counter. This till also backs every future payout — emptying it can leave the house unable to cover the next win.
LanguageData.OWT_HospitalityDetected: Hospitality detected — idle guests may wander off to shop or drink while they're here.
LanguageData.OWT_HospitalityNotDetected: Hospitality not detected — nothing to bridge.
LanguageData.OWT_SettingHospitalityEnabledDesc: An idle Hospitality guest may patronize an open business the same way a travelling customer does. They never rent one of your hotel rooms — Hospitality is already housing them.
LanguageData.OWT_SettingHospitalitySilverDesc: Top up a Hospitality guest's purse the same way an arriving customer's is, if they aren't already carrying enough to buy anything. Turn this off to only let guests spend silver they already have.
LanguageData.OWT_HospitalityBridgeEngaged: {0} wandered over from where they're staying and did business at {1}.
LanguageData.OWT_LetterStickupText: A band from {0} is riding in on the tills, led by someone going by {1}.\n\nThey aren't here to browse. They'll head straight for whatever silver is sitting uncollected and clear out once it's gone — unless somebody gives them a reason to think twice first.
LanguageData.OWT_TillRobbed: {0} cracked the till at {1} and got away with {2}.
LanguageData.OWT_StickupResisted: The stickup turns into a gunfight — the {0} are cutting their losses and running.
LanguageData.OWT_StickupDeparted: The outlaws from {0} have cleared out of town.
LanguageData.OWT_AlertStickupRiskDesc: Uncollected silver is piling up in your tills. The richer they get, the likelier an armed band comes to empty them. Collect your takings, or keep a sheriff on duty to slow the risk.
LanguageData.OWT_SettingStickupsEnabledDesc: Rich, uncollected tills draw armed robbers who empty them and leave unless resisted. Turn this off to remove the risk entirely.
LanguageData.OWT_LetterCoachText: The stagecoach kept to its route: {0} customers from {1}, right on schedule for a {2} line.
LanguageData.OWT_LetterCoachVIPText: {0} stepped off the coach from {1} carrying considerably more silver than the rest of the party.
LanguageData.OWT_RouteTierUpText: The town's name has earned it a better route: {0} is running through here now.
LanguageData.OWT_RouteTierDownMessage: The route has slipped back to {0} — the town's name isn't what it was.
LanguageData.OWT_RouteTierLostMessage: The stagecoach line has stopped running here — appeal has fallen too far to hold a route at all.
LanguageData.OWT_DepotMaxTierLine: Running at the top of the line.
LanguageData.OWT_DepotNoRoute: No scheduled route yet — needs {0} appeal to start one.
LanguageData.OWT_LetterGoldRushText: Word of a strike nearby is spreading fast, and prospectors are already pouring into town. Expect roughly three times the usual custom for the next while, carrying fatter purses too — but nearly all of them are after the same handful of things: tools, medicine, meals, and a stiff drink.\n\nStock the right shelves and the boom pays for itself several times over. Push prices past what's reasonable while it lasts, though, and word travels just as fast — customers remember being gouged long after the vein runs dry.
LanguageData.OWT_GoldRushBustBegins: The vein is drying up. Prospectors are thinning out, and the ones still buying expect ordinary prices again.
LanguageData.OWT_GoldRushBoomStatus: Prospectors are pouring in, chasing tools, medicine, meals and drink above everything else on the shelf. {0} days left before the vein starts to dry up.
LanguageData.OWT_GoldRushBustStatus: The rush has moved on, and custom has slowed to a trickle. It picks back up once the town's reputation climbs to {1} — it's {0} now.
LanguageData.OWT_GoldRushGougeWarning: {0} is gouging the rush, and word is getting around. It's costing the town's good name.
LanguageData.OWT_LetterGoldRushRecoveredText: The town's name has recovered from the rush. Trade is back to its ordinary pace.
LanguageData.OWT_SettingGoldRushEnabledDesc: A nearby strike floods the town with prospectors for a season, then leaves trade quiet until the town's name recovers. Turn this off to remove the event entirely.
LanguageData.OWT_RivalUndercutStartMessage: {0} has slashed its prices to pull trade your way.
LanguageData.OWT_RivalUndercutEndMessage: {0}'s price war has ended; their prices are back to normal.
LanguageData.OWT_RegionalLeadGainedMessage: Your town is now the region's biggest draw.
LanguageData.OWT_RegionalLeadLostMessage: A rival town has pulled ahead of you in regional trade.
LanguageData.OWT_SettingRivalTownsEnabledDesc: One or two NPC towns compete for the same regional trade — your share of it slows your own arrival clock.
LanguageData.OWT_SettingTelemetryEnabledDesc: Logs one line per customer arrival, nightly settlement and stickup roll to the player log — the real numbers this mod's own tuning constants are still guesses about. Off by default; meant for testing, not ordinary play.
